messages:
Devin L: Hey @people-ops — had a baby last week! 🎉 Open enrollment already passed, how do I add my newborn to medical/dental/vision? Is there a deadline?
Sarah (People Ops): Congrats Devin!! :tada: You can add a dependent for a qualifying life event (QLE). Birth is a QLE — you have 30 days from the date of birth to enroll them.
Devin L: Awesome, thanks. What paperwork do you need?
Sarah (People Ops): We need one of the following: birth certificate, hospital birth record, or adoption paperwork. If you have the dependent's SSN, include that too (not required right away but helps). Upload via Rippling or email benefits@redwood.com if you prefer.
Devin L: Does coverage start from the date of birth or from the enrollment date?
Sarah (People Ops): Coverage is effective retroactive to the date of birth as long as you enroll within the 30-day window and provide docs. So claims from birth should be covered.
Raj K: Quick question — my kid turns 26 in July, do I need to do anything to remove them?
Sarah (People Ops): For dependents aging out, coverage generally ends the last day of the month they turn 26. We’ll send a notification ~30 days prior, but you can remove them earlier in Rippling. They’ll get COBRA eligibility info if they qualify.
Mike T: If I got married earlier this year but missed the 30 days to add my spouse, can that be corrected now?
Sarah (People Ops): Marriage is also a QLE but the 30-day rule still applies. If it’s been >30 days, we can’t make a mid-year change unless there’s another QLE. You can wait for open enrollment or submit a request to benefits@redwood.com — sometimes exceptions are made with supporting docs but they’re rare.
Benefits Bot: Friendly reminder: next Open Enrollment window is Nov 1–15. Mark your calendar! https://benefits.redwood.com/open-enroll-2024
Devin L: Thanks — last nit: do I need to update my HSA/FSA contributions when adding a dependent?
Sarah (People Ops): Yes, you can adjust HSA/FSA elections during a QLE (within the same 30-day window). If you increase your HSA mid-year, your payroll will pro-rate contributions. Ask payroll@redwood.com if you want a contribution estimate.
Raj K: If I remove my dependent and they become COBRA-eligible, how long does COBRA last?
Sarah (People Ops): For aging-out, COBRA duration is up to 36 months for the dependent in most cases. COBRA administration details and rates will be sent by our vendor within a week of the qualifying event.
Devin L: Perfect. I’ll upload the birth certificate to Rippling today. Thanks! :pray:
Sarah (People Ops): Great — ping me if you hit any upload errors. Also DM if you want us to confirm once it’s processed. 
Benefits Bot: Document upload note: accepted file types .pdf, .jpg, .png. Max 10MB.
Mike T: Thanks all — very clear.
Sarah (People Ops): np!
